rows.transcript: Welcome to the Athar Open Agentic Pact, a community proposal from ODA and Aerev. This guided narration walks you through the pact, its community model, six pillars, governance, impact tiers, and the Athar OS roadmap. Use the arrows to move at your own pace.
Section one: The Pact. The Aether Open Agentic Pact is an open commitment between institutions, partners, and platforms to learn, build, and deploy agentic AI for public benefit
It is a community proposal from ODA and AI Rev, designed as a community, not a product. Signatories agree on shared standards, an open plugin approach, and measurable real-world outcomes

Section two: The community model. Every webinar, chapter event, and challenge should lead somewhere real, so the model is built around four outcomes for every participant. Learn agentic AI, build a useful agent through the builder journey and marketplace, deploy it through a named accountable institution, and measure a real-world benefit with baseline evidence of time saved, better service, or wider reach

This is a managed global program, not a social channel. A community director, country chapter leads, and a governance council run it against a published calendar. Every activity has an owner, a target, and a report, so membership means participation in a working system rather than a mailing list

Discord is the always-on home of the community. Chapters, cohorts, and office hours live in structured channels with clear moderation and escalation. It is where builders ask questions, showcase agents, and find collaborators between events, governed, searchable, and open to every member

Country chapters bring the pact to life locally. Each chapter adapts the shared curriculum to its language and institutions, hosts events, and connects local builders with government and industry partners. Wave one starts with the UAE base plus two countries, then scales through the roadmap

Webinars, boot camps, and institutional academies form the learning ladder. Webinars introduce agentic AI, boot camps build working agents in days, and academies embed the practice inside ministries, universities, and companies. Every step issues evidence a learner can carry into the marketplace.

Challenges, showcases, and the annual summit turn learning into visible results. Time-boxed challenges solve real institutional problems, showcases publish validated agents, and the global summit reports the year's outcomes to funders and governments in one place

Weekly office hours and tiered support keep builders unblocked. Level one answers common questions in the community. Level two brings platform engineers, and level three escalates to ARF specialists. Institutions on a license receive committed response times.

The builder journey runs from an idea to a validated agent. Prototype, evaluate, validate, then publish in the agent marketplace with a disclosed intended use, a named owner, and supported languages. Specialist agents can earn revenue share, sustaining the builders who create them

The decision in one page: approve the two-engine model, institutions and community, appoint the community director, select the first anchor institutions, and fund the founding cohort. Everything else on the roadmap follows from these four decisions
Section three: Six pillars. Plugins are the connective tissue. One shared plugin standard so every integration works everywhere
Reusable skills are built once and shared across the community

Open where possible, governed where necessary. Interfaces, curricula, and the plugin standard are open. Identity, data residency, and deployment approvals are governed. The balance lets institutions adopt with confidence while the community keeps building in the open

Cross-model interoperability by design. The Pact does not bind any nation or institution to a single model. Agents, skills, and plugins run across leading models so partners can switch providers, host sovereign models, and stay in control of cost and residency
Universal API licenses are managed by Athar, giving members access without duplicated procurement

Agentic AI for all, not for a few. The pact is bilingual by design, accessible by requirement, and priced so a school or clinic can start small. Reach is measured, not assumed, with learners, deployments, and benefits reported by country and by institution
Section four: Pledge and signing. Joining the pact is a simple public commitment

A signatory chooses its roles: sign, govern, build, or learn, and pledges to contribute to at least one of the four participant outcomes. Signing brings access to the learning pathway, the builder journey, and the plugin standard, together with a commitment to report outcomes through the shared impact tiers

Section five: Actors and roles. Institutions, partners, and platforms building the Athar ecosystem together. ODA and AirEv sign and govern with AirEv on demand, E&AI& and Discord building. UNDP, UNICEF, IFRC, WFP, and UNHCR sign and learn. The UAE Ministry of Foreign Trade signs and governs, and the United Arab Emirates governs

Who signs the pact? Institutions sign to deploy validated agents inside accountable workflows, backed by a license, a named owner, and quarterly reporting. Signing gives access to the marketplace, the academies, and the shared plugin standard
Every actor has a clear role: sign, govern, build, or learn.

Who builds on the pact? Developers, practitioners, and student teams build agents and skills through the marketplace with office hours, review, and revenue share for specialist work. Builders keep their intellectual property while publishing under the shared standard

Who learns through the pact? Public servants, teachers, clinicians, farmers, and young people move from foundations to certification. Year one targets ten thousand learners, two thousand five hundred certified, and one hundred facilitators, each recorded against a baseline.
Section six: Governance and roadmap. An open steering council sets the shared plugin standard and approves the roadmap
Decisions, releases, and outcome reports are published so every member can see how priorities are set and how the platform evolves over time
Section seven: Impact and funding
Three impact tiers, one delivery model: access, ownership, legacy. A funder can enter at any tier and climb
Every agreement includes named cohorts and activation targets, independent evaluator baselines, quarterly outcome reports, and open book costs with unspent funds returned
Universal API licenses, marketplace revenue share, and sovereign pilot options fund the model so each partner can choose what fits

Delivered with candidate partners across the humanitarian, development, and technology sectors, shown here for internal review only pending written authorization. Funders receive the same open book reporting as signatories aligned to the three impact tiers

Join the pact. You have seen the agreement, the community model, the six pillars, the actors, the roadmap, the impact tiers, and Athar OS. Now the invitation is yours. Choose your role. Sign, govern, build, or learn. Commit to one real outcome: a learner trained, an agent built, a deployment inside your institution, or a benefit measured. The founding cohort starts this quarter. Open the pledge, add your name, and help us build agentic AI that leaves a lasting trace. This is the Athar Open Agentic Pact. Join us
Section eight, Athar OS
The product tour shows the real screens, the marketplace, the playground, the agent flow builder, and the tools and deployment views captured from the Athar OS wireframes and the launch film
The roadmap runs now in Q4 2026, next in 2027, and later in 2028

Deploy anywhere. Own it. Option A runs software only on your own hardware. Option B is self-hosted in your cloud. Option C is fully managed by AI Rev. Sovereign nodes transfer to national ownership after five to seven years, with local operators trained to run them

Nations empowered. Lebanon, access, one million Lebanese AI experts at $10 million. India, ownership, 100 government schools and 10,000 AI PCs at $13.7 million. Kenya, legacy, a Kenyan-owned sovereign node at around $33 million transferred to a national entity after five to seven years.
